content:
This site now has a knowledge graph. Open any blog article, translation, or book page and click the “Knowledge Graph” tab pinned to the right edge of the screen to see where the current page sits in the site’s knowledge network.

Take the latest post, DeepSeek Harness hands-on notes, as an example: open the article, click the tab on the right, and a drawer slides in with the full site graph. The current article is marked as “here”, with its connections to tags, categories, and linked articles rendered at a glance.

What the panel offers:

Site-wide view: the English graph covers 500+ nodes and 1,100+ relations across blog posts, translations, notices, books, chapters, tags, and categories; the Chinese graph is even larger with 1,800+ nodes and 3,200+ relations.

Locate the current page: the page you are reading is marked automatically, and one click brings the camera back to it.

Explore relations: click any node to see its tags, backlinks, and related articles; book nodes expand into chapter hierarchies, so the next thing to read is one connection away.

Search: find any title inside the panel and select it with the keyboard.

Smooth interaction: wheel zoom, drag to pan, hover to highlight a neighborhood; the computed layout is cached locally, so reopening is near-instant. Dark mode and mobile are both supported.

The graph is generated at build time and only fetched when you open the panel, so regular page loads stay untouched. Alongside the graph, article pages now also show site-wide backlinks — other pages that reference the current article — complementing the graph.

Try the “Knowledge Graph” tab on any article or book page. If you spot two topics that should be connected but are not, let me know in the comments.
